emerging_technology: Generative-AI ambient clinical documentation (ambient scribe): captures clinician-patient conversation and drafts a note for clinician review.
intended_application: Behavioral-health psychotherapy progress-note drafting in outpatient clinics, where narrative nuance, sensitive disclosures, language variation, and patient comfort are central.
organization: A hypothetical small community hospital behavioral-health service with a conservative adoption posture, limited informatics capacity, and high sensitivity to privacy and therapeutic trust.
business_need: Reduce after-hours documentation and clinician burden without degrading note quality or patient interaction.
users_stakeholders: Primary-care clinicians, patients, clinical informatics, privacy/security, health-information management, IT, and operations.
adoption_posture: Conservative/risk-averse; requires local evidence and clinician-led testing before routine use.
capabilities_constraints: Small IT team, mixed EHR templates, limited training/support, needs strong consent, opt-out, access controls, specialty fit, and clinician review.
risk_consequence_context: Mischaracterizing sensitive statements or altering clinical meaning can harm trust and care continuity; human review is mandatory; patients may decline recording.
management_question: Should this service test a tightly bounded opt-in workflow within 12 months, or wait for better specialty-specific evidence?
additional_context: Illustrative educational case, not a claim about a real hospital or local adoption data.
